what: Desktop per-tick sim-cost baseline for the Going Dark 200-unit power budget. The reference a mid-range arm64 device run's `timing-json` output is diffed against — turning 'validate on device' into 'run the matrix, compare these medians'. See docs/platforms.md §6.1 for the schema, the scenario matrix, and the arm64 procedure.

budget_gate.note: The CI perf gate (sim-runner test `stress_200_stays_within_frame_budget`, .github/workflows/test.yml `perf-budget` job) asserts the stress:200 median/p99 stay under these. Deliberately generous vs. the desktop baseline so noise doesn't flap, but a ~5x regression toward the frame budget trips it.

run_schema.description: Each `runs[]` object mirrors the runner's stderr `timing-json` line EXACTLY (same keys, same ms units), so a device line is directly comparable field-for-field. Emitted by sim-runner `TimingStats::json_line`.

keys.scenario: lower-case scene token (round-trips through the sim-runner CLI parser)
keys.ticks: number of timed ticks (N-1 for an N-tick run; tick 0 is the un-timed initial emit)
keys.median_ms: 50th-percentile per-tick step — the stable stat the budget gate compares

device_baselines.note: Mid-range arm64 device numbers are still OWED (the honest Phase 1/3 caveat). Populate this array by running the matrix on a real device per docs/platforms.md §6.1 (scripts/android-stress.sh emits the comparable timing-json), then commit the device object alongside these desktop runs.
